assemblies.name: X-Axis Bench Build
assemblies.description: Assembles the X-axis module from individual parts: seats bearings in the carriage, builds the idler with 5 M6x18 screws and 2 half-bearings, preps the motor holder with belt channel, threads onto guide rods, routes and pegs the belt, and glues the X-axis endstop to the motor holder. Produces a labeled X-axis module ready for fitting between the Y carriages.
assemblies.learningFocus: X-axis carriage uses same bearing fit tests as Y. X-axis idler uses 5 M6x18 screws and 2 half-bearings with flanges out. Motor holder: two nuts in half-piece, belt toothed-side inward, 4 M3x25 motor screws + 3 M6x18 bolts + 1 M6x30 bolt. Second belt peg left loose — tensioned during frame fitting, not at bench.

partGroups.name: X-Axis Carriage Assembly
partGroups.description: Same bearing-in-carriage procedure as Y axes. Middle holes must fit together as pictured. M6x18 bolts at top, M6x30 bolts at bottom. Run shake test and rod-slide test.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: X-axis carriage assembled and bearing fit verified.

partGroups.name: X-Axis Idler Assembly
partGroups.description: X-axis idler uses 5 M6x18 screws and 2 half-bearings (not full bearings). Place bearings with flanges out. Put nuts beside bearings in their slots — these nuts attach the X-axis to the Y-axis carriages later. Add 2 M6x18 bolts through the half-piece, close and tighten fully.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: X-axis idler assembled with nuts in place for Y-carriage attachment.

partGroups.name: X-Axis Endstop Attachment
partGroups.description: Slides X-axis endstop into holder crevice. Super glues holder to top-left and bottom-left motor-piece holes. Adds reinforcing glue along edges. Labels axis X-Axis. Verifies X and Y axes will fit together before setting aside.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: X-axis complete: endstop glued, QC passed, axis labeled and dry-fitted to Y axes.

partGroups.name: X Axis Complete Axis Unit
partGroups.description: The fully assembled x axis axis unit, ready for staging. Contains all bench-built components: carriage, idler, motor holder, rods, and belt.

partGroups.name: X-Axis Motor Holder Assembly
partGroups.description: Places pulley on motor shaft with thin spacer, tightens first set screw, removes spacer, tightens second set screw until pop. Preps motor half-piece with one M6x30 bolt (bottom-left hole, poking up) and three nuts. Places belt toothed-side inward in belt channel of other half. Closes halves gently. Inserts motor with cable plug facing bottom-right. Tightens 4 M3x25 motor screws Â¾ tight then 3 M6x18 bolts. Performs dangle test.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: X-axis motor holder assembled and dangle-tested.

partGroups.name: X-Axis Axis Rod Assembly
partGroups.description: Inserts the two guide rods into the completed idler (rods flush with idler bottom), slides the carriage onto the rods (long bolt ends closer to idler), then pushes the motor holder onto the rods (motor facing the carriage bolt heads). Tightens the idler's two shorter bolts. Checks rods are still flush with idler bottom.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: X-axis guide rods threaded through idler â†’ carriage â†’ motor holder with rods flush at idler.

partGroups.name: X-Axis Belt Threading
partGroups.description: Inserts one belt end through the larger carriage belt hole, routes it around the idler bearing (slight curve helps), pulls through the smaller carriage belt hole. Threads through first peg (foot facing away from axis center), inserts belt end ~Â¾ inch and pushes peg into ribbed hole. Places second peg loosely â€” it will be tightened after frame mounting when the full belt length is confirmed.
partGroups.milestoneMessage: X-axis belt routed and first peg locked. Second peg loose for frame-side tensioning.

steps.name: Lay out axis pieces
steps.instructionText: Gather and lay out all axis pieces: two carriage half-pieces, two idler half-pieces, two motor holder half-pieces, the stepper motor, both guide rods, and all hardware (M3x25 screws, M6x18 and M6x30 bolts, nuts).

steps.name: Clean excess plastic from holes
steps.instructionText: Use a box cutter or cordless power drill to clear excess plastic from all semi-circle rod holes in the carriage, idler, and motor holder half-pieces. Holes must be smooth so rods insert freely and belts do not rub.

steps.name: QC: verify all plastic pieces are clean
steps.instructionText: Verify: each carriage half has 4 clean semi-circles, each motor holder half has 6, each idler half has 8. All M6 bolt holes and M3 screw holes are clear of extra plastic.

steps.name: Place 4 bearings in carriage half
steps.instructionText: Place four linear bearings into one carriage half-piece with the flanges facing outward (away from each other).

steps.name: Shake test: bearings must not rattle

guidance.instructionText: Hold both carriage halves firmly together and shake the assembly.
guidance.whyItMattersText: Compress the two halves by hand until there is no gap. Shake side-to-side and up-down for 2–3 seconds. No tools needed — this is a hand-compression test only. Tip: grip a completed carriage from another axis as a tactile reference for correct feel.

validation.successCriteria: No audible rattle or tactile movement from the bearings.
validation.failureCriteria: Bearings click, rattle, or shift inside the halves when shaken.

feedback.successMessage: Bearings are snug. Proceed to the rod slide test.
feedback.failureMessage: Bearing fit is too loose. Swap to a slightly larger LM8UU or try the next batch of bearings. Re-test before closing the carriage.

steps.name: Rod slide test: slight resistance, not too free

guidance.instructionText: Insert a smooth guide rod through the carriage and hold it so the rod is vertical.
guidance.whyItMattersText: The rod should slide or drop through as you hold the carriage, but there should be a little resistance — it's good if you have to shake the carriage for the rod to slide through. Motors pull 20 lbs of belt force on this carriage, so it should not slip through too fast with no resistance.

validation.successCriteria: Rod slides or drops through with slight resistance. Shaking the carriage helps it move through.
validation.failureCriteria: Rod slides too quickly with zero resistance (too free), OR rod jams and requires force to push (too tight).

feedback.successMessage: Resistance feels correct. Both tests pass — proceed to close the carriage halves.
feedback.failureMessage: Too free: wrap each bearing in one layer of electrical tape to tighten the fit and retest. Too tight: check that bearings are fully seated and carriage halves are not warped.

steps.name: Bolt carriage halves together
steps.instructionText: Secure both halves with M6x18 bolts on top and M6x30 bolts on bottom. Critical alignment: the small ribbed belt hole must sit directly beside the large smooth belt hole. Wrong alignment mismatches the peg holes.

steps.name: Insert M6x18 bolt into idler half
steps.instructionText: Begin assembling the idler: place an M6x18 bolt through one idler half-piece from the outside.

steps.name: Stack two flanged bearings onto bolt
steps.instructionText: Insert two bearing pieces one on top of the other onto the bolt, flanges facing outward (away from each other).

steps.name: Align idler rod holes before closing
steps.instructionText: Hold the second idler half against the first and confirm the circular rod holes on both halves line up correctly before pressing them together.

steps.name: Bolt idler halves and secure bearing
steps.instructionText: Secure the idler with an M6x18 bolt through the top and one M6x30 bolt in the belt-side hole. Tighten until firm.

steps.name: Gather endstop switch and holder piece
steps.instructionText: Gather the endstop microswitch and its 3D-printed holder piece. This endstop step applies to this axis only.

steps.name: Slide endstop board into holder crevice
steps.instructionText: Slide the endstop board into the crevice of the holder piece. The switch arm must face toward the arrowhead direction of the holder, away from the mounting legs. The bottom of the board should be flush with the bottom of the holder.

steps.name: Super glue endstop into holder
steps.instructionText: Dab super glue along the side edges of the crevice. Do not apply glue to the metal switch arm or any board contacts.

steps.name: Prep motor holder holes for endstop
steps.instructionText: Dab super glue into the two motor holder holes facing the belt (top-left and bottom-left when the motor faces you).

steps.name: Press endstop holder onto motor holder
steps.instructionText: Press and hold the endstop holder piece firmly against the motor holder piece for at least 30 seconds until bonded.

steps.name: Reinforce endstop joint with super glue
steps.instructionText: Add super glue along all joint edges between the endstop holder and the motor holder to strengthen the connection.

steps.name: Stage completed X axis on bench
steps.instructionText: The X axis is fully assembled — carriage sides, idler, motor holder, rods, belt, and endstop are complete. Place the assembled X axis at the staging position on your bench. Label it before setting down.

steps.name: X-axis bench QC, dry-fit to Y axes, and label
steps.instructionText: QC checklist: carriage moves smoothly along axis rods; rods flush with idler bottom; idler and carriage bolt heads on same side; toothed side of belt inward; belt pegs in correct holes; belt peg holes line up. Dry-fit the X-axis against the completed Y axes and confirm it will fit. Label axis X-Axis with masking tape.

steps.name: Mount pulley on motor shaft with spacer
steps.instructionText: Rest the thin spacer on the motor housing, then seat the pulley on the shaft above it. Tighten the first set screw with an Allen key â€” the spacer keeps the pulley off the housing.

steps.name: Lock pulley set screw until it pops
steps.instructionText: Remove the spacer. Tighten the second set screw as firmly as possible, pressing near the Allen key midpoint. A soft "pop" means fully seated. Whether or not you hear it, tighten as hard as you can.

steps.name: Load motor holder half with nuts and M6x30 bolt
steps.instructionText: Orient the motor holder half with the rectangular belt channel facing you. Insert one M6x30 bolt and three nuts into the holes now â€” the motor will cover them and block access later.

steps.name: Insert belt in motor holder channel
steps.instructionText: Insert the belt into the channel in the motor holder half-piece with the toothed side facing inward toward where the pulley will sit.

steps.name: Close motor holder halves together
steps.instructionText: Press the two motor holder halves together with the belt seated in the channel.

steps.name: Confirm belt runs smoothly on pulley
steps.instructionText: Hold the motor in position against the holder and give the belt a gentle pull â€” it should slide along the motor pulley. If it does not, reseat the belt in the channel.

steps.name: Attach motor with 4 M3x25 screws
steps.instructionText: Insert the first M3x25 motor screw and tighten 3/4 of the way. Insert the remaining three screws and tighten each the same way â€” leave slightly loose so the motor retains flex for belt tensioning later.

steps.name: Insert M6x18 bolts into motor holder
steps.instructionText: Insert M6x18 bolts into the three remaining holes of the motor holder, threading each into its embedded nut. Hand-snug for now — the next step uses the drill.

steps.name: Tighten motor holder M6x18 bolts with drill
steps.instructionText: Tighten each of the 3 motor-holder M6x18 bolts into its embedded nut using the electric drill. The motor holder is now fully clamped to the holder pieces.

steps.name: Dangle test: motor holder hangs securely
steps.instructionText: Hold the complete motor assembly by one of its bolts. It should hang without wobble or separation. This confirms bolts are fully seated before rod insertion.

steps.name: Insert rods into idler, ends flush
steps.instructionText: Insert both guide rods into the completed idler piece. Rod ends must be flush against the bottom of the idler. If rods are hard to insert, loosen the idler bolts, slide rods in, then re-tighten.

steps.name: Tighten short idler bolts onto rods
steps.instructionText: Tighten the two shorter idler bolts with an electric drill to grip the rods firmly. Leave the longer bolt loose â€” it will be used to attach the axis to the frame.

steps.name: Slide carriage onto rods
steps.instructionText: Slide the already-assembled X-axis carriage onto the rods with the long bolt ends closer to the idler. The carriage was built earlier in the X-axis carriage stage — no new parts to place.

steps.name: Push motor holder onto rods
steps.instructionText: Push the motor holder piece onto the rods so the motor faces the carriage bolt heads. Loosen bolts if needed to slide on, then re-tighten.

steps.name: QC: rods flush, carriage slides freely
steps.instructionText: Check that rod ends are still flush at the idler bottom. Slide the carriage the full rod length â€” it should move with only slight bearing resistance.

steps.name: Thread belt through large carriage hole
steps.instructionText: Inspect the carriage: one belt hole is large and smooth, the other small and ribbed. Insert one belt end through the large smooth hole with the toothed side facing inward.

steps.name: Route belt around idler bearing
steps.instructionText: Feed the belt around the bearing inside the idler. Tip: curve the belt slightly in the direction of travel first â€” it navigates around the bearing more easily.

steps.name: Thread belt back through small carriage hole
steps.instructionText: Once the belt is around the idler bearing, pull it back through the smaller ribbed carriage hole.

steps.name: Confirm belt peg orientation before locking
steps.instructionText: Thread the belt end through a belt peg. Confirm: the foot of the peg faces away from the toothed side of the belt and away from the axis center. Wrong orientation prevents the peg from locking correctly.

steps.name: Lock first belt peg
steps.instructionText: Insert the belt end approximately 3/4 inch into the small ribbed belt hole, then simultaneously insert the peg into the same hole and press firmly until it locks.

steps.name: Insert second peg loosely
steps.instructionText: Insert the second peg directly across from the first. Hand-tighten the belt by pulling it through the first peg as much as you can easily. Leave the second peg loose â€” it will be fully tensioned after mounting to the frame.

steps.name: Travel test: carriage moves smoothly with belt
steps.instructionText: Slide the carriage along the full rod length with the belt installed. It should move smoothly without binding. If it binds, check the belt is not twisted and both carriage holes are correctly threaded.

steps.name: Label completed X-Axis Axis and set aside
steps.instructionText: Use masking tape and a marker to label this assembly as "X-Axis Axis". Set it aside in a safe place. It is complete and ready for frame mounting.

hints.title: Six-point QC + dry-fit to Y axes
hints.message: X-axis QC has six points: carriage slides smoothly; rods flush at idler; bolt heads same side; belt toothed side inward; belt pegs in correct holes; belt peg holes line up. Also dry-fit the X-axis against both Y-axis carriages and confirm it will span correctly before labeling.
